what_this_is: A length of annealed copper wire, specified as a resistivity and a geometry rather than as a resistance.
why_these_numbers: 16.78 nOhm.m at 20 degC and 3930 ppm/K are the standard annealed-copper figures. Stating the wire as rho, L and A rather than as R_ref means the reference resistance is computed twice, independently, and a cross-section or length fault is visible.
evidence_level: LEVEL 3 - reference data for the copper coefficients; LEVEL 5 for the algebra.
derivations_left_to_the_adapters: reference resistance R_ref = resistivity * length / cross_section
